title: Feed a captive nut under channel lips
context: A fastener in an enclosed channel must enter through the open end. Its wide head must finish under both retaining lips. This tests a constrained assembly path while the other arm braces the loose channel.
scoring: Channel rotation above 5 degrees also scores zero. Entry requires nut tilt and yaw below 5 degrees. Entry credit clears if the nut centre leaves x 250 mm to 270 mm or y negative 100 mm to positive 100 mm. It also clears if nut height differs from its entry height by 8 mm or more or tilt or yaw leaves that limit. Score zero if the channel centre ever moves more than 5 mm from its starting position or if the nut goes more than 5 mm below the table. The nut must pass the front entry gate with x within 5 mm of 260 mm and y between negative 85 mm and negative 55 mm and its lower face within 6 mm of z 757.5 mm. This earns 0.25. After entry a nut x within 6 mm of 260 mm and y between negative 20 mm and 66 mm with the wide head upper face below z 786.5 mm earns 0.5. A seated nut must have x within 4 mm of 260 mm and y within 5 mm of 60 mm and its lower face within 4 mm of z 757.5 mm. Tilt and yaw must be below 5 degrees. It must move below 8 mm per second and 0.1 radians per second. This earns 0.75. Both measured grippers open beyond 35 mm raises this to 1.0. Full success must hold for 2 seconds. All other outcomes score zero.
fidelity: The channel and nut are rigid printed polymer solids. The broad nut head physically fits below both rigid lips. There is no threaded engagement or screw tightening. The long nut handle gives the gripper access above the lips. Contacts use PhysX defaults with a 1 mm contact offset. No elastic material deformation is simulated.
instruction: Hold the grey channel still. Feed the blue T nut through its open front end and slide it to the white end mark. The wide head must be below both retaining lips. Release both grippers. Keep the channel within 5 mm of its starting position. All equipment is unpowered.
setup: Use the official bimanual YAM station. The tabletop is at z 747.5 mm. x points forward. y points left. z points up. All props are rigid PA12 polymer prototypes. All joint positions start at zero. The channel has an initial outer envelope of 92 by 330 by 47 mm. Its authored root is at x 260 mm and y 30 mm and z 747.5 mm. Its initial yaw is 0.0 radians. Its mass is 0.6 kg. Its root is free to move. The nut has an initial outer envelope of 44 by 30 by 63 mm. Its authored root is at x 170 mm and y -190 mm and z 762.5 mm. Its initial yaw is 0.0 radians. Its mass is 0.035 kg. Its root is free to move. The mark has an initial outer envelope of 90 by 3 by 1 mm. Its authored root is at x 260 mm and y 60 mm and z 748 mm. Its initial yaw is 0.0 radians. Its root is fixed to the tabletop. The inventory lists each collider and body mass and joint anchor and travel limit. Local solid positions are measured from the named body root. Outer envelope sizes describe the reset pose.
run_limit: 2400 control steps at 20 Hz. This is 120 seconds of control time.
reset_notes: Restore every object to the starting pose in scene_inventory.json and every joint to zero. Nothing is consumed. Use one epoch with seed 0 and object_jitter=0.
